title.en: Japan earthquake: What we know so far

summary.en: Japan is currently experiencing the aftermath of a significant earthquake that struck Kyushu island, with ongoing reports detailing the situation.
summary.zh: 日本九州岛遭受强烈地震袭击，目前正在应对其影响，相关情况正在持续更新。

body.en:
Nineteen people are missing at an Aeon shopping centre and a paper factory after the 6.8 magnitude earthquake hit Kyushu island, an official said.

The quake has also caused power cuts, damaged roads, collapsed a castle wall and destroyed a footbridge.

The quake hit the Kumamoto prefecture on Kyushu island at 16:27 local time (07:27 GMT) on Tuesday, with hundreds of thousands of people being told to move to evacuation shelters.

The Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) reported the earthquake had a magnitude of 7.1, which the US Geological Survey later measured as a 6.8. Quake magnitude figures are often updated as seismologists obtain and analyse new data.

Kumamoto - where the collapsed Aeon Mall is located - is a city on the Kyushu island of Japan.

The southern island of Kyushu is the third-largest of the four main islands in Japan, and the second most populous.

A total of 278 people were killed in 2016 by powerful quakes in Kumamoto and neighbouring Oita prefectures, according to Japan's public broadcaster NHK.

People remain trapped inside an Aeon Mall in Kumamoto prefecture, the fire service said.

Ten people remain unaccounted for at the shopping centre, an official at the Disaster Management Division of Kumamoto prefecture told the BBC.

Four people have been rescued from the mall and their lives are "not in danger", the official added.

A witness reported seeing an explosion and smoke at the shopping mall after the quake.

The witness saw the second floor of the building collapse, with some shoppers taken to hospital.

Japan's fire and disaster management agency later confirmed that the second floor of a "commercial facility" collapsed, with many people trapped inside.

Elsewhere in the Kumamoto prefecture, a chimney reportedly collapsed at Nippon Paper's Yatsushiro Plant, according to police, who are being cited by NHK.

An aerial photograph of the site obtained by Reuters news agency appears to show a broken and collapsed chimney.

The disaster management official told the BBC that two people at the plant had been found in a state of "cardiac arrest" and nine people are still missing.

Tremors also caused historic walls at the 17th-century Kumamoto castle to tumble.

It is not the first time the castle has succumbed to an earthquake. When a 7.3 magnitude quake hit the region in 2016, parts of the 400-year-old castle were also damaged as turrets and curved walls collapsed.

It is unclear if anyone was injured, or when the collapse took place. Traffic appears to be travelling on the bridge that runs parallel to it.

More than 40,000 households are without power, according to an update on Kyushu Electric's website. There has also been damage to roads.

There was no notice or training exercise in place. Felt like warning shots or attempted intimidation On the crisis in prison places, this has been a long time coming. title.en: 'It's a hell of a situation': Spain grapples with devastating wildfires
title.zh: 西班牙与毁灭性野火搏斗，情况“如同地狱”

summary.en: Spain is currently battling devastating wildfires, with three fires in the Madrid region causing particular concern. A new heatwave is anticipated to hit the country from Wednesday, exacerbating the challenging conditions.
summary.zh: 西班牙目前正在与毁灭性的野火作斗争，马德里地区的其中三场火灾尤其令人担忧。预计从周三开始，新一轮热浪将袭击西班牙，使严峻的局势进一步恶化。

body.en:
For the past week, firefighters have been tackling a series of wildfires ravaging the Spanish countryside, threatening dozens of communities and forcing more than tens of thousands of people to evacuate their homes.

Three fires in the Madrid region have caused special concerns, with a new heatwave expected to hit Spain from Wednesday, fuelling fears that firefighting efforts could be hindered.

"It's a hell of a situation," said Madrid regional leader Isabel Díaz Ayuso, as she visited affected areas on Monday alongside Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez.

Sánchez spoke on Tuesday of highly challenging hours and days ahead but of light beginning to appear "at the end of the tunnel".

Temperatures are expected to approach 40C in some regions in the coming days, with the heatwave forecast to last at least until Sunday.

Spain's state meteorological agency Aemet has warned the "fire danger level will continue to rise to extreme levels, hindering firefighting efforts".

Regional authorities began lifting some evacuation and lockdown orders on Tuesday as conditions improved - including in parts of the Madrid region - but restrictions remain in place in the worst-affected areas.

In the Madrid region alone, more than 56,500 people have been evacuated since the fires broke out last week. A further 27,797 people have been ordered to stay at home.

Ayuso had earlier described the wildfires as "the biggest natural catastrophe in the history of Spain".

She wrote on X that the situation was now "improving little by little" and some residents may soon be allowed to return home.

Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska told Spain's La 1 TV channel that firefighting efforts on Monday night had resulted in "relatively positive progress".

"This morning, we are very satisfied with the work done. We are going to consolidate the work that has been done," he said.

He maintained that "we must be positive; we have the emergency under control" but conceded that "weather conditions are not helping us at all".

Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez announced on Tuesday that areas affected by the wildfires have been declared "disaster zones".

title.en: Mysterious deaths of 14 elephants in Kenya prompts urgent inquiry
title.zh: 肯尼亚14头大象神秘死亡引发紧急调查

summary.en: It is the highest number of elephant deaths to be recorded in this area of southern Kenya in decades.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
An urgent investigation has been launched into the mysterious deaths of 14 elephants in southern Kenya near the Amboseli National Park.

The Kenya Wildlife Service (KWS) told the BBC that experts were examining the carcasses and said that tissue samples had been sent to laboratories to determine whether the deaths were caused by disease, poisoning or another factor.

The park and its surrounds are known as the Amboseli ecosystem, a vast area that straddles the border with Tanzania, which is famous for its wildlife.

Officials say this is the first time in decades that elephant mortalities on this scale have been recorded in the region where they have successfully cracked down on poaching.

The carcasses include elephants of different ages and sexes, suggesting the deaths are not limited to a single family or demographic.

The wildlife agency's head of communication, Duncan Wanyama, told local media the bodies had been found at different locations surrounding the Amboseli National Park, around 15km (nine miles) to 30km from its boundaries.

According to figures from the Amboseli Trust for Elephants, which monitors the movements of the animals, there were more than 2,000 elephants in the Amboseli ecosystem as of 2025.

body.en:
Firefighters in France are working around the clock to contain wildfires that have been raging in the Gironde region, while bracing for another sharp rise in temperatures.

"The fire is like David against Goliath," said Eric Brocardi, spokesman of the national firefighters' federation.

Four of his colleagues had died in recent weeks across France, he said, and 2,000 had been deployed in the Gironde to contain the flames, which for days have ravaged the countryside between the coastline and Bordeaux.

According to regional prefect Sophie Brocas 14 places that had already been hit by the fires saw new flare-ups on Tuesday. "We are not in the clear," she said.

This summer's fourth heatwave was expected to start by Wednesday, bringing temperatures in the area to 40C.

Dozens of communities are still threatened by wildfires that forced more than 70,000 to evacuate their homes over the last week - although many have now been allowed back.

The Madrid region has been especially affected, but Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said while there were highly challenging hours and days ahead, light was beginning to appear "at the end of the tunnel".

In neighbouring Portugal, 400 firefighters were tackling a large fire on three active fronts in the eastern Guarda area.

The French city of Bordeaux, which has a population of 260,000, is not currently under threat, according to officials, despite the fact that one of the wildfires burning on Monday came only 15km (9 miles) from the city's periphery.

But Commander Rémi Lassoureille, who is leading the firefighting response in the Gironde region, is still worried about the western edge of the wildfire.

"We are frightened about the impact on Bordeaux and the metropolitan area," he said. Air quality in the city also deteriorated greatly.

"By Sunday evening everything had really begun to empty out," a holidaymaker from Essex told the BBC, adding that the air was "really smoky" with bits of ash. "People were staying indoors, so it was eerie, and very sad."

The majority of residents and tourists were wearing masks and the smell of smoke clung on to clothes for days, she said.

A firefighter "got a round of applause" as he walked through the Marché des Chartrons in Bordeaux where restaurants were having to close their doors because of the ash in the air, she added.

"The city has been very quiet," said Graham White, president of the Bordeaux British Community. "The shops, restaurants and cafes are fairly empty... Interestingly on Sunday when there was still smoke, there were people brave enough to sit outside on terraces."

body.en:
A French Navy patrol boat appeared to fire a round of gunshots "without warning" in the English Channel during a BBC interview with the UK shadow home secretary.

Conservative MP Chris Philp was being interviewed about small boat crossings by BBC journalist Michael Keohan as a French warship passed by at 09:15 BST (10:15 CET), about three miles from the French coast.

Keohan said there were 17 shots but "no warnings" from the boat about 300m away, which left Philp believing it was an intimidation tactic to "stop us covering migrant crossings".

The French authorities said it was part of a training exercise, unrelated to the presence of a British ship, which it said was out of range of fire.

Philp dismissed this claim as "not credible", adding: "There were no warnings in place about live firing training exercises.

The captain of the fishing boat which hosted the interview, Matt Coker, said he had "never seen anything like it before".

The French authorities said the boat, PSP Flamant, was not engaged in an operation to monitor migrant boats.

Keohan said there were 17 shots, adding: "There was no warning for our boat, no signs given that this was the French's intention."

Philp said it "felt to me like an attempted intimidation to stop us covering migrant crossings".

At sea, Keohan described it as "the most unusual moment... in the quiet of the Channel" when the gunshots rang out mid-interview.

A French patrol officer at the back of the boat was seen pointing a pistol towards the sea. It is believed that is where the shots came from.

Keohan, who was on board the vessel with a reporter from The Times, added: "There was no warning for our boat, no signs given, that this was the French's intention.

After the incident, Philp said: "It is extraordinary that the French Navy will fire live rounds to defend their waters against a visiting British politician but cannot bear to do anything about stopping illegal Channel crossings.

"If France showed people smugglers half the seriousness they showed me, the boats would stop.

"Instead, the French wave them through and pass them off to the British coastguard so it's our problem."

A UK government spokesperson said: "This is a matter for the French authorities."

The French authorities said a handgun shooting exercise had taken place by the public service patrol boat Flamant off the coast of Cap de Gris-Nez.

A spokesperson said: "In order to maintain their high level of operability in the current international context, the units of the French Navy train regularly.

title.en: EU civil protection mechanism: Coordinating Europe's firefighters
title.zh: 欧盟民事保护机制：协调欧洲消防员

summary.en: French President Emmanuel Macron has activated the EU civil protection mechanism to help combat devastating wildfires. The system has become increasingly effective, yet it will reach its limits in the summer of 2026.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
French President Emmanuel Macron has activated the EU civil protection mechanism to help combat devastating wildfires. The system has become increasingly effective, yet it will reach its limits in the summer of 2026.

France is quite well-prepared for wildfires. The government operates 12 Canadair water bombers and eight Dash firefighting aircraft. In addition, leased aircraft and helicopters are being used.

However, the fleet is currently needed simultaneously across many parts of the country. A drought has been intensifying for weeks, and several heat waves with temperatures sometimes exceeding 40 degrees Celsius (104 Fahrenheit) have left the vegetation extremely parched. The devastating wildfire near Bordeaux on the Atlantic coast has already engulfed more than 42,000 hectares of forest and vegetation.

At the same time, fires and follow-up extinguishing efforts in southern and southeastern France  are tying up additional emergency personnel. In many places, firefighters are battling the flames in an exhausting, round-the-clock effort. However, strong winds are fanning the fire fronts, making them almost unstoppable, and more than 220,000 people have had to leave their homes and vacation homes so far.

The gravity of the situation is also underscored by the fact that the French government has deployed an A400M military transport aircraft equipped for aerial firefighting for the first time. The A400M can drop around 20 metric tons of fire retardant, more than three times as much as a Canadair.

Nevertheless, the situation is currently so dire that President Emmanuel Macron also activated the EU civil protection mechanism (CPM) and requested assistance from other European countries.

To activate the CPM, a country reports its needs to the European Union's emergency response coordination centre, ERCC, in Brussels . ERCC experts assess which of the 37 participating countries can provide assistance.

Initial assistance for France was mobilized within a few hours and has since been significantly expanded. Firefighting aircraft and helicopters from Portugal , Croatia , the Czech Republic , Germany , Turkey , Sweden  and Slovakia  are supporting France, primarily in the greater Bordeaux area.

At the same time, however, the EU also dispatched six additional firefighting aircraft from Greece , Turkey and Italy to Spain . This means that 13 of the 22 firefighting aircraft available for this summer have already been mobilized for these two countries. The figures also demonstrate how quickly the European reserve can be drawn upon when multiple large-scale wildfires occur simultaneously. title.en: Poland: Top court rejects recognizing EU same-sex marriages

summary.en: Poland's constitutional court has overturned plans to recognize same-sex marriages that took place in other EU member states. This defies an order from the EU's top court and could set up a clash on the matter.

title.en: Could US airstrikes stop insurgency in Mali?
title.zh: 美国空袭能否阻止马里叛乱？

summary.en: US President Donald Trump is reportedly considering airstrikes against the Al-Qaeda-linked JNIM in Mali. Analysts suggest that while such attacks might weaken the jihadist group, they would not resolve the underlying core issues of the conflict.
summary.zh: 据多方报道，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普正在考虑对马里与基地组织有关联的JNIM发动空袭。分析人士指出，此类袭击或许能削弱圣战分子，但无法解决核心问题。

body.en:
US President Donald Trump is considering airstrikes against the Al-Qaeda-linked JNIM in Mali, according to multiple reports. Analysts say such attacks might weaken the jihadists but would not address the core issues.

For years, Mali has struggled to contain a growing jihadist insurgency , particularly in the country's northern region. Following the withdrawal of French troops and despite the authorities' close cooperation with Russia , the al-Qaeda-linked Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM) continues to expand its influence. Now, a new actor could enter the conflict: the United States (US) .

Founded in 2017, JNIM unites several Islamist groups under the banner of al-Qaeda . Over the past years, the organization has developed into the most powerful jihadist force in the Sahel . Its objective is the establishment of an Islamist order and the displacement of state structures as well as Western influence.

"We are no longer talking about a group that only carries out isolated attacks," explains Tobias Rüttershof, head of the Sahel Program of the Konrad Adenauer Foundation (KAS), which is affiliated with Germany's CDU party and has an office in Mali, in an interview with DW. "In many regions, JNIM effectively controls the security situation, collects taxes, mediates local conflicts and in some areas is more present than the Malian state." 

According to the US National Counterterrorism Center, JNIM was responsible for more than 1,200 deaths in 2025, making it the second-deadliest terrorist organization in the world. Particularly concerning is the group's geographic expansion: JNIM is now active not only in Burkina Faso and Niger , but increasingly in the coastal states of West Africa. 

The US government is divided over the question of direct military strikes. Supporters such as Sebastian Gorka, senior director for counterterrorism at the National Security Council, argue that JNIM is one of the world's most dangerous jihadist organizations and that its advance must be halted.

Russia's security strategy in Mali has so far failed to deliver results, according to Rüttershof. 

"After the withdrawal of French forces, the UN mission MINUSMA , and European training missions, Mali's military government argued that  Russia could stabilize the security situation more effectively," Gorka told DW. "That expectation has not been fulfilled so far. On the contrary, JNIM appears stronger today than it was several years ago."

Following military coups in 2020 and 2021, Bamako increasingly distanced itself from Western partners and expanded cooperation with Russia.

The Malian government has responded cautiously to reports of possible US airstrikes.

title.en: Will Pakistan intervene amid Houthi attacks on Saudi ships?
title.zh: 巴基斯坦会干预胡塞武装袭击沙特船只吗？

summary.en: Pakistan and Saudi Arabia are strategic defense partners, but experts say there are limits to how far Islamabad can go in opposing Iran-backed Houthis.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Pakistan and Saudi Arabia are strategic defense partners, but experts say there are limits to how far Islamabad can go in opposing Iran-backed Houthis.

Pakistan condemned attacks on Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea by Iran-backed Yemeni Houthi militia  last week as the conflict in the Middle East threatens to expand.

In a statement, the Pakistani Foreign Ministry warned that any Houthi threat to Pakistani maritime interests in the Red Sea could be met with the "lawful use of force."

Pakistan enjoys a trade and security relationship with Saudi Arabia, and Pakistani-flagged vessels frequent Saudi ports in the Red Sea. Last September, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia signed a mutual defense agreement that contains a "collective security" clause, meaning attack on one country is considered an attack on both.

After the Houthis launched missiles at southern Saudi Arabia last week, Pakistan's Foreign Ministry expressed its "unwavering commitment" to the security pact.

At the same time, Pakistan also has ties with Iran, and has been a key mediator between Tehran and Washington to end the Iran war.

Any military act against the Iran-backed Houthis could place Islamabad in one of the most complicated foreign policy situations it has faced in years.

Historically, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan have shared close military and strategic relations. Pakistani military generals and advisers have aided the kingdom for decades.

Farea Al-Muslimi, a Yemen expert at London-based think tank Chatham House, told DW that Pakistani troops are already in Yemen in support of the Saudis, "carrying out security and training-related duties alongside Saudi forces."

Nevertheless, if Houthi attacks on oil tankers and commercial shipping escalate in the Red Sea, Saudi Arabia could turn to Pakistan for help.

"Pakistan is one of Riyadh's closest defense partners, and their mutual defense pact makes such a request plausible. Having also come under Iranian attack, Saudi Arabia may increasingly look to Islamabad for military assistance if it feels under growing security pressure," Michael Kugelman, senior fellow at the Washington-based Atlantic Council, told DW.

However, Pakistan's improving ties with Iran and its mediation to end the US-Iran conflict could complicate any Pakistani military role on Saudi Arabia's behalf. 

"Pakistan and Iran have a complicated relationship based on the calculation of tactical gains by either side. In any case, Pakistan has warned Iran several times that in case of conflict it will support Saudi Arabia," Ayesha Siddiqa, a Pakistani military analyst and senior fellow at King's College London, told DW.

body.zh: 巴基斯坦和沙特阿拉伯是战略防御伙伴，但专家表示，伊斯兰堡在反对伊朗支持的胡塞武装方面能走多远是有限的。 由于中东冲突有可能扩大，巴基斯坦谴责伊朗支持的也门胡塞民兵上周在红海袭击沙特油轮。 巴基斯坦外交部在一份声明中警告说，胡塞武装对巴基斯坦在红海的海上利益的任何威胁都可以通过“合法使用武力”来应对。 巴基斯坦与沙特阿拉伯有着贸易和安全关系，悬挂巴基斯坦国旗的船只频繁出入红海的沙特港口。去年9月，巴基斯坦和沙特阿拉伯签署了一项共同防御协议，其中包含“集体安全”条款，这意味着对一个国家的攻击被视为对两个国家的攻击。 胡塞武装上周向沙特阿拉伯南部发射导弹后，巴基斯坦外交部表达了对该安全协议的“坚定承诺”。 与此同时，巴基斯坦也与伊朗有联系，并一直是德黑兰和华盛顿之间结束伊朗战争的关键调解人。 任何针对伊朗支持的胡塞武装的军事行动都可能使伊斯兰堡陷入多年来面临的最复杂的外交政策局势之一。 历史上，沙特阿拉伯和巴基斯坦有着密切的军事和战略关系。数十年来，巴基斯坦军事将领和顾问一直在援助该国。 伦敦智库查塔姆研究所的也门专家法雷亚·穆斯利米（Farea Al-Muslimi）告诉德国之声，巴基斯坦军队已经在也门支持沙特，“与沙特军队一起执行安全和训练相关的职责”。 然而，如果胡塞武装在红海对油轮和商业航运的袭击升级，沙特阿拉伯可能会向巴基斯坦寻求帮助。 华盛顿大西洋理事会高级研究员迈克尔·库格曼（Michael Kugelman）告诉德国之声：“巴基斯坦是利雅得最亲密的防务伙伴之一，他们的共同防御协议使这一要求变得合理。沙特阿拉伯也受到伊朗的攻击，如果它感到安全压力越来越大，它可能会越来越多地向伊斯兰堡寻求军事援助。” 然而，巴基斯坦改善与伊朗的关系以及为结束美伊冲突而进行的调解可能会使巴基斯坦代表沙特阿拉伯发挥的军事作用变得复杂化。 伦敦国王学院高级研究员、巴基斯坦军事分析家阿耶莎·西迪卡 (Ayesha Siddiqa) 告诉德国之声：“巴基斯坦和伊朗之间的关系很复杂，双方都会考虑双方的战术收益。无论如何，巴基斯坦已多次警告伊朗，如果发生冲突，它将支持沙特阿拉伯。” 2024年，伊朗和巴基斯坦经历了前所未有的紧张局势，伊朗和巴基斯坦相互进行了跨境导弹袭击，此后这两个邻国开始重建……

title.en: Tsunami warnings issued for southern Japan after major earthquake

summary.en: Thousands of homes are without power, and a tsunami warning was issued after an earthquake shook Japan's southern Kyushu island.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
An earthquake with a preliminary magnitude of ‌7.1 has struck Japan's southern Kumamoto prefecture, knocking out power to ‌thousands of homes, stopping rail services and triggering warnings for tsunamis and ‌aftershocks.

Companies including Sony and TSMC, the world's largest contract chipmaker, have plants in the area of the quake.

The ‌Japanese government ‌issued emergency ⁠earthquake warnings on Tuesday for Kumamoto, Nagasaki, Kagoshima, Fukuoka, Saga, Oita, and Miyazaki prefectures, all on Japan's southern Kyushu island.

A tsunami warning for a wave measuring one metre was briefly issued after the earthquake, the Japan Meteorological Agency said.

Japan is one of the world's most earthquake-prone ⁠countries, with a tremor occurring at ‌least every five minutes.

Located along the "Ring of Fire" of volcanoes and oceanic trenches partly encircling ‌th Pacific Basin, Japan accounts for about 20 per cent of the world's earthquakes of magnitude 6.0 or more.

A massive earthquake in Kumamoto 10 years ago killed 275 people and injured a further 2739, according to an official count.

Kyushu Electric Power said about 40,000 homes ‌had lost power as a result of the quake, while railway company JR Kyushu said it had suspended services, including its high-speed bullet trains.

title.en: 'Cannot go unanswered': Iran's latest test is a country already at war

summary.en: Threats of retaliation risk converging two ongoing conflicts, raising concerns about escalating violence in the region.

body.en:
Ukraine's attack against an Iranian cargo ship in the Caspian Sea has sparked fears of a widening conflict and the convergence of two major wars.

Iran has vowed it will retaliate against Ukraine after its president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, said his military carried out long-range strikes in the Caspian Sea against vessels transporting military cargo involving Iran on Sunday.

Iran says Ukraine's "hostile and criminal" act and subsequent explosion against what it said was a commercial vessel killed one sailor and injured another, and its foreign minister Abbas Araghchi vowed the attack "cannot go unanswered".

The incident marks the first time the two sides, who are already fighting wars of their own — Ukraine against Russia and Iran against the United States — have come to a potential confrontation.

Ukrainian officials say the vessel was carrying components for drones and missiles from Iran to Russia. Iranian counterparts, however, said the vessel was "entirely civilian" and carrying "no military cargo".

Ukraine's foreign minister, Andrii Sybiha, denounced Iran's threats of retaliation as "unjustified and groundless".

"The regime in Tehran is a direct accomplice to Russian aggression against Ukraine, fuelling Moscow’s criminal war with weapons that have killed Ukrainians since 2022," he said.

Iran is a major supplier to Russia of its deadly, cheap Shahed drones, which have been used in the war in Ukraine, especially in the earliest phase.

"They were technology that Russia hadn't didn't have in its own arsenal at the time," Adam Lockyer, an associate professor in strategic studies at Macquarie University, told SBS News.

"Its dependency upon Iranian drone technology has decreased over time, but still, you can see that those two parties have been helping each other and mutually supporting each other where they can."

On Sunday, Zelenskyy also said Russia was handing Iran its satellite observations of Gulf states and US military sites, to assist its strikes in the Middle East.

"There is a clear correlation between Russia's satellite imagery of these sites and Iranian strikes," he said.

Ukraine said its strike was part of a wider attack against a Russian oil field and a Russian missile boat on that day.

The waterway's location is also significant: Iran has been relying on its northern routes, including the Caspian Sea, to circumvent a US naval blockade.

The timing of the incident is also significant. Zelenskyy is due to meet with US President Donald Trump in Washington on Wednesday.

summary.en: Fighting between the United States and Iran has been paused since the weekend. While President Trump expressed optimism for a potential deal, Iran has maintained its stance and denied any peace talks.

body.en:
United States President Donald Trump has voiced optimism at the prospect of a negotiated peace deal with Iran, as the two sides held their fire for a third consecutive day.

Fighting between the longtime foes has been paused since Saturday after 13 nights of renewed US strikes on the Islamic republic sparked by a breakdown in diplomacy over Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.

But the US leader expressed hope on Tuesday that renewed diplomacy could bring an end to the war that began in late February with a wave of US-Israeli strikes, rattling both the region and the global economy.

"I have a lot of patience ... We'll see what happens," he said aboard Air Force One.

Iran had earlier denied that there were any direct talks with the US to end the conflict.

"Mediators may convey messages from the American side to us regarding current developments in the region. But at present, we are not engaged in any negotiations with the United States," said Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei.

Trump told the US news outlet Axios that mediating countries had asked him to hold fire to give diplomacy a chance, adding: "We are in very deep talks with Iran."

Aboard Air Force One, he said that if the new efforts failed, "we go back to doing what we were doing" before the pause in fighting.

On that subject, he dismissed concerns that US ammunition stockpiles were running low nearly five months after war broke out.

"We have a lot of ammunition. We have a lot of the mid-level stuff too, more than we could ever use no matter what," he said.

Despite the recent lull, Saudi Arabia came under attack on Monday, with its defence ministry saying it had intercepted several drones fired by Iran-linked groups in Iraq targeting oil facilities.

No group claimed responsibility, but the Saudis called on Baghdad to prevent such attacks from being launched from its territory.

Pakistan, which has been mediating a resolution to the Middle East war, condemned the drone attacks, saying they "pose a grave threat to peace and stability" in the region.

Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels also said they launched drone attacks on Saudi Arabian oil infrastructure in response to incursions by the kingdom's drones. Saudi Arabia is yet to comment on the claim.

Saudi Arabia and other Gulf nations accused pro-Iran militias in Iraq of launching waves of attacks on their territory during the conflict's earlier phase, but the groups haven't claimed any attacks in the region since the resumption of hostilities.

Elsewhere, the Israeli military, which has not joined the recent fighting, said it had intercepted two drones near the Jordanian border...

As hundreds of thousands of people flee fast-moving wildfires across Europe, Australians heading overseas are being urged to stay informed, monitor official travel advice and understand what their travel insurance covers if their plans change.

More than 330,000 people have been evacuated across France and Spain as fires burn through popular holiday destinations, closing roads, delaying flights and forcing communities to flee. Authorities have also issued fresh evacuation orders near the historic Spanish city of Toledo, while firefighters continue battling major blazes around Bordeaux in southwestern France.

The fires have intensified during Europe's busy summer holiday period, with airports, major roads and tourist destinations among those affected as emergency services race to contain the blazes.

In France, more than 220,000 people have been evacuated as wildfires continue to burn through the Gironde region, home to vineyards, coastal towns and the popular tourist destination of Cap Ferret.

French interior minister Laurent Nuñez described the situation as "very unfavourable", warning the fire was moving towards Bordeaux, although authorities have so far ruled out evacuating the city itself.

The blaze came within about 15km of Bordeaux's outskirts over the weekend, prompting police to go door-to-door in nearby communities to evacuate residents.

Travel has also been disrupted, with Bordeaux Airport reporting widespread delays after air traffic restrictions were introduced to allow firefighting aircraft to operate safely.

Spain is also grappling with multiple major blazes, with more than 115,000 people evacuated and another 30,000 ordered to shelter in place.

The largest fire, in the central province of Ávila, has burned more than 50,000 hectares, making it the country's biggest wildfire in recent history. Fires continue to burn near Madrid and in the eastern province of Castellón.

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has announced a civil protection emergency will be declared in the affected central regions, unlocking additional recovery funding.

More than 150,000 hectares have burned across Spain since the start of the year — six times the area destroyed over the same period last year.

Australian travellers are being urged not to panic, but to closely monitor conditions, remain flexible and understand what their travel insurance does — and doesn't — cover if their plans are disrupted.

May those shaping this future prioritize building up humanity over merely accumulating power...
reflection.zh: 关于人工智能未来发展的持续辩论及其所造成的行业分歧提醒我们，仅有知识是不够的。尽管技术进步力量强大，但雅伟的话语表明，真正的智慧是将知识与爱和对他人的关怀精神相结合。愿那些塑造这一未来的人，优先考虑造福人类，而非仅仅积累权力和利润。

verse.textEn: Knowledge puffs up while love builds up.
verse.textZh: 知识是叫人自高自大，惟有爱心能造就人。

title.en: Britain promised to protect Hongkongers from China. Why does it now seem ready to sacrifice them? | Nathan Law
title.zh: 英国承诺保护香港人免受中国侵害。为什么它现在似乎准备牺牲他们？ |罗冠聪

summary.en: Activists under threat from Beijing are facing strange difficulties with UK immigration. Their safety must not be traded for warmer relations with China Nathan Law is a pro-democracy activist and former legislator from Hong Kong. He is currently a political refugee in the UK As...
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en: Activists under threat from Beijing are facing strange difficulties with UK immigration. Their safety must not be traded for warmer relations with China Nathan Law is a pro-democracy activist and former legislator from Hong Kong. He is currently a political refugee in the UK As authoritarian countries such as Russia, China and Iran are more active in engaging in long-arm strategies to silence their critics in the UK, transnational repression is garnering more attention. It is right that the Metropolitan police and other British law enforcement agencies have specific units and mechanisms to counter it. But it takes more than just confronting this long-distance repression to make political dissidents of these authoritarian countries feel safe in the UK, and the UK government is not living up to expectations. The threat is real. Members of the Hongkonger community have received threats from the Chinese regime – some have had threatening letters, some people were deepfaked into sexual content, some even had families questioned and arrested back home. With the level of this targeting linked to the deterioration of Hong Kong politics, many have utilised the humanitarian pathway enabled by the previous government to relocate. Continue reading...
body.zh: 受到北京威胁的活动人士在英国移民问题上面临着奇怪的困难。不能用他们的安全来换取与中国关系的缓和。罗冠聪是一位民主活动人士，也是香港前立法会议员。他目前是英国的政治难民。随着俄罗斯、中国和伊朗等独裁国家更加积极地采取长臂战略来压制英国的批评者，跨国镇压正在引起更多关注。伦敦警察厅和其他英国执法机构确实有专门的单位和机制来应对。但要让这些独裁国家的政治异见人士在英国感到安全，仅仅面对这种远程镇压是不够的，而英国政府并没有达到人们的期望。威胁是真实的。香港人社区的成员受到了来自中国政权的威胁——有些人收到了恐吓信，有些人被深度伪造色情内容，有些人甚至在国内遭到盘问和逮捕。由于这种目标的程度与香港政治的恶化有关，许多人利用前任政府允许的人道主义途径搬迁。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This story draws attention to justice, dignity, and accountability. Micah 6:8 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with justice tempered by mercy, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到公义、尊严与问责。Micah 6:8提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以带着怜悯的公义来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: What does Yahweh require of you? To act justly and to love mercy and to walk humbly with your God.
verse.textZh: 雅伟向你所要的是什么呢？只要你行公义，好怜悯，存谦卑的心，与你的神同行。

title.en: Hong Kong activist allowed to stay in UK after deportation threat
title.zh: 香港活动人士在被驱逐出境威胁后获准留在英国

summary.en: Wu was detained for hours at London's Heathrow Airport last week and refused entry, he told the BBC.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Former Hong Kong opposition leader Wu Chi-wai has been allowed to stay in the UK with his family for six months, after initially being detained at the border.

Wu had arrived at London's Heathrow Airport last Wednesday, where he was detained for nearly 10 hours and initially refused entry, he told BBC Chinese. He said he was later told he could stay for only one week, after which he would have to report to the airport to be deported.

But on Monday, the UK Border Force approved his entry and granted him a standard stay of six months, he said.

The 63-year-old was the leader of the now-defunct Democratic Party and one of the most recognisable faces of the city's quashed pro-democracy movement.

Wu is one of the so-called Hong Kong 47, a group of high-profile pro-democracy leaders who were sentenced to jail after a controversial national security trial.

He was released in June after spending more than five years in prison for subversion and other convictions.

Wu told BBC Chinese that his son and wife moved to the UK in 2022 and 2023, and the only communication he had with them since then was through monthly phone calls and letters. He had hoped to reunite with his family in the UK during his recent visit, he added.

Ahead of his departure, Wu said he had consulted staff at the British Consulate General in Hong Kong, asking if there would be any problems with his entry.

"The information I received was that there would be none," he said, adding that consular staff said they would explain his criminal record and itinerary to the UK Border Force.

The Border Force said he was not considered a "genuine visitor" who was solely visiting family, he said.

Wu denies that he had intended to apply for political asylum in the UK - a claim that was previously reported in the media.

Rights group Hong Kong Watch, which had called on UK authorities to allow Wu to stay in the country, said in a statement that it welcomed the recent news.

"This is the right outcome, and it should never have taken this long," Megan Khoo, Hong Kong Watch's policy director, said in a statement on Monday.

"He should never have faced the prospect of removal back to the city that jailed him."

Wu was using his British National (Overseas) (BNO) passport - a special travel document issued to Hong Kong permanent residents before 1 July 1997, when Hong Kong returned to Chinese rule - to enter the UK.

BNO passport holders are typically allowed to stay in the UK visa-free for six months.

Since 2021, the UK government launched a visa programme for BNO passport holders. Those granted the visa are eligible to work, study and live in the UK, putting them on a pathway to citizenship after they settle in the UK.

The new policy came after Hong Kong was rocked by massive pro-democracy protests,...
body.zh: 香港前反对党领袖胡志伟最初在边境被拘留后，现已获准与家人在英国居留六个月。 吴告诉BBC中文网，他于上周三抵达伦敦希思罗机场，在那里被拘留了近10个小时，并最初被拒绝入境。他说，后来他被告知他只能停留一周，之后他必须到机场报到才能被驱逐出境。 但他说，周一，英国边境部队批准了他的入境，并给予他六个月的标准居留期限。 这位 63 岁的老人是现已解散的民主党领导人，也是该市被镇压的民主运动中最知名的面孔之一。 吴是所谓的“香港47人”之一，这是一群备受瞩目的亲民主领导人，他们在一次有争议的国家安全审判后被判入狱。 他因颠覆罪和其他罪名入狱五年多，并于六月获释。 吴告诉BBC中文，他的儿子和妻子于2022年和2023年移居英国，此后他与他们唯一的交流就是通过每月的电话和信件。他补充说，他希望在最近的访问期间与英国的家人团聚。 吴说，出发前曾咨询英国驻香港总领事馆工作人员，询问他入境是否会遇到任何问题。 他说：“我收到的信息是不会有任何人。”他补充说，领事馆工作人员表示，他们将向英国边境部队解释他的犯罪记录和行程。 他说，边防部队表示，他不被视为只是探望家人的“真正访客”。 吴否认他曾打算在英国申请政治庇护——此前媒体曾报道过这一说法。 人权组织“香港观察”曾呼吁英国当局允许吴留在该国，该组织在一份声明中表示，对最近的消息表示欢迎。 “这是正确的结果，不应该花这么长时间，”香港观察政策总监邱梅根 (Megan Khoo) 周一在一份声明中表示。 “他不应该面临被遣送回监禁他的城市的前景。” 吴当时使用他的英国国民（海外）（BNO）护照 - 1997年7月1日香港回归中国统治之前向香港永久居民签发的特殊旅行证件 - 进入英国。 BNO 护照持有者通常可以免签证在英国停留六个月。 自2021年起，英国政府针对BNO护照持有人推出了签证计划。获得签证的人有资格在英国工作、学习和生活，这使他们在英国定居后踏上了获得公民身份的途径。 这项新政策是在香港受到大规模民主抗议活动震动之后出台的……

reflection.en: This story draws attention to peace-making and restraint. Matthew 5:9 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with mercy, truth, and restraint, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到和平与克制。Matthew 5:9提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以怜悯、真实与节制来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.
verse.textZh: 使人和睦的人有福了，因为他们必称为神的儿子。

title.en: ‘We have lost everything’: extreme rainfall across Asia brings flash floods and typhoons
title.zh: “我们失去了一切”：亚洲极端降雨引发山洪和台风

summary.en: Extreme rainfall across Asia has led to widespread flash floods and typhoons, causing immense devastation from Afghanistan to Taiwan. The unprecedented deluge highlights the severe impact of climate breakdown, with one construction worker describing 10 days and nights of non-stop rain and the loss of everything.
summary.zh: 亚洲各地遭遇极端降雨，引发大范围山洪和台风，从阿富汗到台湾都遭受了巨大破坏。这场前所未有的洪灾凸显了气候崩溃的毁灭性影响，一名建筑工人描述了连续十天十夜的降雨，以及他们失去了一切的困境。

body.en: From Afghanistan to Taiwan, unprecedented deluge highlights devastating impact of climate breakdown “It rained for 10 days and 10 nights, non-stop – I’d never seen anything like it,” says Anar Gul, a construction worker who lives in the remote district of Dur Baba in eastern Afghanistan. The houses in his village are built from stone and mud, which makes them extremely vulnerable to heavy rains. After days of rain, Gul’s kitchen collapsed and his neighbour, Sayed Afsar Sadat, saw a large part of his house completely destroyed. “Rains like this are coming heavier and earlier each year,” says Sadat. “They are destroying the roads and washing away our crops. It’s impacting us directly.” Continue reading...
body.zh: 从阿富汗到台湾，史无前例的洪水突显了气候崩溃的破坏性影响。居住在阿富汗东部杜巴巴偏远地区的建筑工人阿纳尔·古尔 (Anar Gul) 说：“这场雨持续了 10 天 10 夜，不间断，我从来没有见过这样的情况。”他村里的房子都是用石头和泥土建造的，这使得它们极易受到大雨的影响。经过几天的降雨，古尔的厨房倒塌了，他的邻居赛义德·阿夫萨·萨达特 (Sayed Afsar Sadat) 看到他的房子的很大一部分完全被毁。 “像这样的降雨每年都来得更大、更早，”萨达特说。 “他们毁坏了道路，冲走了我们的庄稼。这直接影响着我们。”继续阅读...

reflection.en: The widespread devastation from extreme rainfall across Asia reminds us of creation's deep distress. As the earth groans under the weight of unprecedented deluges, we are called to acknowledge the suffering of both the land and its inhabitants. In these moments of profound loss, we hold onto the hope that Yahweh hears the cries of creation and those who...
reflection.zh: 亚洲各地极端降雨造成的广泛破坏，提醒我们受造界正经历着深切的痛苦。当地球在史无前例的洪灾重压下呻吟时，我们被呼召去承认土地及其居民所承受的苦难。在这些深重损失的时刻，我们紧紧抓住雅伟垂听受造界和那些失去一切之人的呼求的盼望。

verse.textEn: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.
verse.textZh: 我们知道，一切受造之物一同叹息、劳苦，直到如今。

title.en: China's new challenge as natural disasters strike - fake AI videos
title.zh: 自然灾害来袭，虚假AI视频成中国新挑战

summary.en: Storms and flooding incidents over the last few months have seen fake AI-generated videos inundating social media in China.
summary.zh: 近几个月来，中国遭受了风暴和洪灾，导致社交媒体上充斥着大量人工智能生成的虚假视频。

body.en:
As China deals with the fallout of Typhoon Noul that made landfall over the weekend, officials will be painfully aware that they will likely have an additional challenge to deal with: dangerously misleading videos created with Artificial Intelligence (AI).

Powerful storms and flooding incidents over the last few months have seen fake videos inundating social media platforms – these include images of dead bodies floating in floodwaters, the false depiction of severe flooding in areas actually not affected and others with blatantly fake details of emergency response efforts.

In some areas, videos containing false information about power outages prompted residents to panic buy emergency supplies.

Flooding in Hengzhou city, Guangxi in early July caused hundreds of snakes to escape from a breeding farm. Then fake images were also published showing crocodiles being released into a river.

In an already tense and dangerous situation involving mass evacuations and complex rescue operations, authorities want to avoid panic. Now they fear that AI technology - which China is pouring billions of dollars into - is providing simple, accessible tools that can be used to trick the public.

"Many of these content creators use disaster news to try to gain followers, knowing that more sensational or exaggerated content will garner more likes and more views. They are deliberately fabricating information to grab people's attention," Huang Zhihua, Deputy Chief in charge of online public security for Zhejiang Police Department told Chinese state media.

In recent weeks, there have been arrests and punishment – ranging from detention awaiting criminal prosecution to fines – for the creation of bogus reports and video content.

But experts are warning that an unprecedented crisis of misinformation could be looming.

In an article published by the newspaper of the Communist Party's Central Party School, Professor Chen Bin said, "AI dramatically lowers the technical barriers to producing false information. Individuals no longer require sophisticated technical skills. By simply prompting AI tools, they can rapidly generate convincing text, images, audio and video… which is highly realistic but entirely fabricated content, manufactured on a large scale."

Professor Gao Fuping, from the East China University of Political Science and Law, told the BBC that motivation for the publishing of such false content ranges from those who do it "to create something amusing without thinking about the consequences", to those who want to "generate traffic for personal gain" or those who wish to deliberately "cause panic or social unrest".

"Some users think the online world is anonymous and unregulated or that they cannot be traced," he said.

There have been calls for all AI-generated...
body.zh: 当中国应对周末登陆的台风诺尔的影响时，官员们将痛苦地意识到他们可能还要应对额外的挑战：用人工智能（AI）制作的危险的误导性视频。 过去几个月发生的强烈风暴和洪水事件导致社交媒体平台上充斥着虚假视频——其中包括漂浮在洪水中的尸体的图像、对实际未受影响地区严重洪水的虚假描述，以及其他公然虚假的应急响应工作细节。 在一些地区，包含有关停电的虚假信息的视频促使居民恐慌购买应急物资。 7月初，广西衡州市发生洪水，导致数百条蛇从养殖场逃出。随后还发布了一些假图片，显示鳄鱼被释放到河里。 在涉及大规模疏散和复杂救援行动的紧张和危险局势中，当局希望避免恐慌。现在，他们担心中国正在投入数十亿美元的人工智能技术正在提供简单、易于使用的工具，可用于欺骗公众。 浙江省公安厅网络公安分管副局长黄志华对中国官方媒体表示，“许多内容创作者利用灾难新闻来吸引关注者，因为他们知道更耸人听闻或夸张的内容会获得更多点赞和浏览量。他们故意捏造信息来吸引人们的注意力。” 最近几周，有人因制作虚假报告和视频内容而遭到逮捕和处罚，从等待刑事起诉的拘留到罚款。 但专家警告说，一场前所未有的错误信息危机可能即将来临。 陈斌教授在中共中央党校报刊发表的文章中表示，“人工智能极大地降低了制造虚假信息的技术门槛，个人不再需要高深的技术技能，只需人工智能工具的提示，就可以快速生成令人信服的文字、图像、音频和视频……这些内容高度真实，但完全是捏造的、大规模制造的内容。” 华东政法大学教授高福平告诉BBC，发布此类虚假内容的动机包括“为了制造一些有趣的事情而不考虑后果”，到“为个人利益产生流量”或故意“引起恐慌或社会动荡”。 “一些用户认为网络世界是匿名的、不受监管的，或者他们无法被追踪，”他说。 有人呼吁所有人工智能生成的......

reflection.en: In times of crisis, when natural disasters strike, the rapid spread of misinformation, especially through fake AI videos, can add to public distress. Proverbs 14:15 reminds us to be discerning, not simply believing everything we encounter, but thoughtfully considering the information before us. Cultivating prudence helps us navigate a complex digital...
reflection.zh: 在危机时期，当自然灾害发生时，虚假信息，特别是人工智能生成的虚假视频的迅速传播，会增加公众的痛苦。箴言14:15提醒我们要有辨别力，不要轻易相信我们所遇到的一切，而是要审慎思考摆在我们面前的信息。培养审慎的态度有助于我们驾驭复杂的数字环境，并明智地应对挑战。

verse.textEn: The simple believe anything, but the prudent give thought to their steps.
verse.textZh: 愚蒙人是话都信；通达人步步谨慎。

title.en: Cars swept away and trees toppled as Typhoon Noul brings flooding to southern China – video
title.zh: 台风“诺尔”带来洪水，汽车被冲走，树木被连根拔起——视频

summary.en: Typhoon Noul made landfall in southern China, bringing heavy rain and strong winds to Guangdong province. Authorities predict continuous torrential rain, as the storm is the strongest to hit China in 2026 so far.
summary.zh: 台风“诺尔”在中国南方登陆，给广东省带来了强降雨和大风。当局预计大到暴雨将持续到周二，这是2026年迄今为止袭击中国的最强风暴。

body.en: Typhoon Noul made landfall early on Sunday in southern China, bringing heavy rain and gale-force winds across Guangdong province. Authorities said heavy to torrential rain would continue until Tuesday. The rapidly developing storm is the strongest to hit China so far in 2026, according to state media. It has forced the relocation of more than 715,000 people in Guangdong province, authorities said on Sunday. Typhoon Noul forces more than 715,000 from homes and cancels hundreds of flights in China and Hong Kong Continue reading...

In such moments of natural upheaval, we are reminded that Yahweh is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in trouble. reflection.zh: 当台风“诺尔”带来强风和洪水时，社区面临着巨大的挑战和不确定性。在这样的自然动荡时刻，我们被提醒雅伟是我们的避难所和力量，是我们在患难中随时的帮助。即使地动山摇，我们也能在祂坚定的同在中找到慰藉。

verse.textEn: God is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in trouble.
verse.textZh: 神是我们的避难所，是我们的力量，是我们在患难中随时的帮助。

title.en: ‘I thought it didn’t stand a cat’s chance in hell’: Andrew Ridgeley on Wham’s surreal trip to China
title.zh: ‘我以为它根本没有一丝希望’：安德鲁·里奇利谈威猛乐队超现实的中国之旅

summary.en: Four decades after Wham! became the first Western pop act to tour China, Andrew Ridgeley reflected on the surreal experience, including silent gigs and awkward embassy receptions. He also recalled the “bloody ludicrous” hiring of Lindsay Anderson as director for the 1985 trip.
summary.zh: 威猛乐队成为首个在中国巡演的西方流行乐队四十年后，安德鲁·里奇利回顾了那次超现实的经历，包括沉默的演出和尴尬的使馆招待会。他还回忆起1985年那次旅行中“荒谬至极”地聘请林赛·安德森担任导演。

body.en: Four decades after he and George Michael became the first western pop act to tour the country, Ridgeley recalls silent gigs, awkward embassy receptions – and the ‘bloody ludicrous’ hiring of Lindsay Anderson as director Wham! special – read about George Michael’s great lost superstar duets album There has always been something surreal about Wham!’s 1985 trip to China. George Michael and Andrew Ridgeley looked like alien visitors on the streets of Beijing, their bouffant hair and flamboyant outfits setting them apart from the Mao jackets and drab uniforms of the Chinese people they encountered. Now the full strangeness of the duo’s brief trip, which made them the first western pop act to play in the country, is explored in a fascinating documentary film, Wham! 10 Days in China. Using previously unseen archive footage and featuring new interviews with many of the people involved in the tour, it shows the extraordinary impact Wham!’s two concerts had on their Chinese audience, as well as providing a snapshot of a country on the brink of great change. title.en: Berlin Pride: Latest in string of deadly vehicle attacks
title.zh: 柏林骄傲游行：最新一起致命车辆袭击事件

summary.en: A vehicle attack at a Berlin Pride event is the latest in a series of incidents where vehicles have been used as weapons, with similar attacks reported in the US, Canada, and China in recent years.
summary.zh: 柏林骄傲游行活动中发生的一起车辆袭击事件，是近年来车辆被用作武器的系列事件中最新的一起，美国、加拿大和中国也曾发生过类似的袭击。

body.en:
The attack at a Berlin Pride event is only the most recent incident on a long list where vehicles were used as weapons. The US, Canada, and China also saw similar attacks in recent years.

A Christopher Street Day event in the German capital, which attracts thousands of people every year, was attacked on Saturday night by a 21-year-old suspect who police said was associated with the "Islamist scene" in Berlin. One person was killed and another 16 people were injured, while the suspect, named as Abdul B., fled the scene.

Two people were killed and 20 more injured in early May when a car drove through a crowd in the eastern German city of Leipzig. The suspect in the case was described as a 33-year-old German national and local resident, who had been known to police, though not for relevant offenses.

At least two people were killed and several were injured in the southwestern German city of Mannheim in 2025 when a motorist intentionally drove his car into a crowd of people , according to police and public prosecutors. Authorities identified the suspect as a 40-year-old German man. Law enforcement ruled out a political motive at the time, though the man had paid a fine under Germany's hate crime laws for a comment he made on a social media platform in 2018.

A 37-year-old woman and her two-year-old daughter were killed in Munich in February last year when a car was rammed into a demonstration organized by the trade union Verdi. A 25-year-old Afghan man subsequently went on trial for their murder, as well as the attempted murder of the dozens of other people injured in the attack. 

A vehicle plowed into a crowd of New Orleans revelers early on New Year's Day 2025, killing 14 people and injuring dozens of others. The driver of the vehicle and two police officers were killed in a firefight soon after the attack, which took place at about 3:15 in the morning local time. The FBI said it was investigating the incident as an act of terrorism.

At least six people died and more than 300 were injured when a man slammed a rented BMW SUV into a Christmas market in eastern Germany. The suspect, who was arrested at the scene, was a 50-year-old doctor originally from Saudi Arabia who had expressed anti-Muslim views and support for the far-right AfD party. In June 2026, he was sentenced to life in prison, with the court noting the severity of his crime, which more or less rules out the possibility of an early release.

A 62-year-old driver  rammed a small SUV into people exercising at a sports complex in southern China on November 11, 2024, killing 38 people in the country's deadliest act of mass homicide in years. Another 48 were injured. Authorities said the perpetrator was upset...
body.zh: 柏林骄傲活动中的袭击只是一长串将车辆用作武器的事件中的最新一起。近年来，美国、加拿大和中国也发生过类似的攻击。 德国首都的克里斯托弗街日活动每年都会吸引数千人参加，周六晚上，该活动遭到一名 21 岁嫌疑人的袭击，警方称该嫌疑人与柏林的“伊斯兰主义现场”有关。造成 1 人死亡、16 人受伤，嫌疑人 Abdul B. 逃离现场。 5 月初，德国东部城市莱比锡一辆汽车驶过人群，造成两人死亡、二十多人受伤。据描述，该案嫌疑人是一名 33 岁的德国国民和当地居民，警方认识他，但并未因相关罪行而认识他。 据警方和检察官称，2025 年，德国西南部城市曼海姆一名驾车者故意驾车冲撞人群，造成至少两人死亡、多人受伤。 当局确认嫌疑人是一名 40 岁的德国男子。执法部门当时排除了政治动机，尽管该男子因 2018 年在社交媒体平台上发表的评论而根据德国仇恨犯罪法缴纳了罚款。 去年2月，慕尼黑工会威尔第组织的一场示威活动中，一辆汽车被撞，导致一名37岁的妇女和她两岁的女儿丧生。一名 25 岁的阿富汗男子随后因谋杀以及企图谋杀袭击中受伤的其他数十人而接受审判。 2025 年元旦早些时候，一辆汽车冲撞了新奥尔良狂欢者的人群，造成 14 人死亡、数十人受伤。袭击发生在当地时间凌晨 3 点 15 分左右，车辆司机和两名警察在袭击发生后不久的交火中丧生。 联邦调查局表示，正在将此事件作为恐怖主义行为进行调查。 一名男子将一辆租来的宝马 SUV 撞向德国东部的圣诞市场，造成至少 6 人死亡、300 多人受伤。现场被捕的嫌疑人是一名来自沙特阿拉伯的 50 岁医生，曾表达反穆斯林观点并支持极右翼选择党。 2026 年 6 月，他被判处终身监禁，法院注意到他罪行的严重性，这或多或少排除了提前释放的可能性。 2024 年 11 月 11 日，一名 62 岁的司机驾驶一辆小型 SUV 撞向在中国南方一个体育场馆锻炼的人们，造成 38 人死亡，这是该国多年来最致命的大规模凶杀案。另有 48 人受伤。当局表示，肇事者情绪激动……

reflection.en: The repeated use of vehicles as weapons in public spaces highlights the destructive presence of evil in our world. In the face of such acts, Yahweh calls us not to be overcome by evil, but to actively overcome evil with good, fostering safety and compassion.
reflection.zh: 车辆在公共场所被反复用作武器，凸显了我们世界中破坏性邪恶的存在。面对此类行径，雅伟呼召我们不要被恶所胜，而是要积极地以善胜恶，培养安全与怜悯。

verse.textEn: Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
verse.textZh: 你不可为恶所胜，反要以善胜恶。

Almost exactly 200 years ago, in the period 1825-27, a powerful US naval squadron led by Commodore John Rodgers was sent to the Mediterranean to defend American ships from the depredations of Greek corsairs and pirates. For all the new-minted republic’s brave talk of liberty, the US squadron did not assist Greece’s ongoing “regime change” struggle for independence from the Ottoman empire. Its sole, self-serving purpose was to defend US trade, markets and business interests. After abandoning his call for a people’s revolution in Tehran , this, too, is what Trump’s reckless war with Iran has now boiled down to. title.en: US-China AI rivalry heats up as Chinese models gain ground
title.zh: 中美人工智能竞争加剧，中国模型迎头赶上

summary.en: China's AI platforms are rapidly advancing, narrowing the gap with US technology. This progress has led to renewed threats from the Trump administration, alongside accusations of intellectual property theft, raising concerns about escalating tensions between the two nations.
summary.zh: 中国的人工智能平台正迅速缩小与美国同行的差距。这一进展引发了特朗普政府新的威胁，并伴随着知识产权盗窃的指控，令人担忧两国之间的紧张关系可能升级。

body.en:
China's AI platforms are rapidly closing the gap with their US counterparts, prompting fresh threats from the Trump administration. With accusations of intellectual property theft, could tensions boil over?

In what seems like the blink of an eye,  China has gone from being up to five years behind the United States in top-tier artificial intelligence (AI) to lagging by just a few months.

While US players, including Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's ChatGPT , have spent hundreds of billions of dollars to push the frontier of AI, China has pursued a very different path .

Faced with US curbs on high-end chips that help AI to do its most advanced thinking, Chinese tech firms have prioritized dozens of open-source AI models built on "good enough"  technology .

These platforms, including DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen and Xiaomi's MiMo, are now widely deployed across Chinese businesses, government services and consumer devices.

In the latest sign of the gap closing, Chinese startup Moonshot AI last week unveiled Kimi K3, a model that rivals one of the most advanced AI models — Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 — on key benchmarks.

In some tests, Kimi K3 matches or even surpasses Claude with far less computing power and at a fraction of the cost. 

Global technology specialist Alvin W. Graylin thinks Kimi K3's arrival turns high-end AI from an expensive luxury into something practical and affordable.

"For 98% of customers, the 1 to 2% difference [in knowledge] isn't worth paying 10 to 20 times more."

China's latest advance has already drawn a strong reaction from Washington, with US President Donald Trump now threatening to block US access to Chinese AI models.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, meanwhile, warned earlier this week that the US could sanction Chinese models over alleged intellectual property (IP) theft.

Anthropic  and OpenAI have accused Chinese labs of using their models to train their own systems, a process known as distilling.

While distilling is a common practice by AI labs worldwide to a limited extent, the companies say their models have been bombarded with queries to harvest advanced reasoning. The White House warned in April that China was doing it on an "industrial scale."

Beijing has hit back, rejecting the accusations as baseless and calling US threats of sanctions and model bans "technological bullying" to contain China's rise.

Giulia Neaher, a research analyst at the Strategic Foresight Hub at the Washington-based Stimson Center think tank, downplayed the role of distilling in Kimi's progress.

"A great degree [of its success] is due to the talent, infrastructure and the resources that were poured into building this...
body.zh: 中国的人工智能平台正在迅速缩小与美国同行的差距，引发了特朗普政府的新威胁。随着知识产权盗窃的指控，紧张局势会升级吗？ 似乎一眨眼的功夫，中国在顶级人工智能 (AI) 领域就从落后美国五年变为仅落后几个月。 尽管包括 Anthropic 的 Claude 和 OpenAI 的 ChatGPT 在内的美国企业已经花费了数千亿美元来推动人工智能的前沿发展，但中国却走了一条截然不同的道路。 面对美国对帮助人工智能实现最先进思维的高端芯片的限制，中国科技公司优先考虑了数十种基于“足够好”技术的开源人工智能模型。 这些平台，包括 DeepSeek、阿里巴巴的 Qwen 和小米的 MiMo，现已广泛部署在中国企业、政府服务和消费设备中。 作为缩小差距的最新迹象，中国初创公司 Moonshot AI 上周推出了 Kimi K3，该模型在关键基准测试上可与最先进的人工智能模型之一——Anthropic 的 Claude Fable 5 相媲美。 在某些测试中，Kimi K3 可以与 Claude 相媲美甚至超过 Claude，但其计算能力却要低得多，而成本却只是 Claude 的一小部分。 全球技术专家 Alvin W. Graylin 认为 Kimi K3 的到来将高端人工智能从昂贵的奢侈品变成了实用且负担得起的东西。 “对于 98% 的客户来说，[知识] 1% 到 2% 的差异并不值得多付 10 到 20 倍的费用。” 中国的最新进展已经引起华盛顿的强烈反应，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普现在威胁要阻止美国使用中国的人工智能模型。 与此同时，财政部长斯科特·贝森特本周早些时候警告称，美国可能会因涉嫌盗窃知识产权而制裁中国模型。 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 指责中国实验室使用他们的模型来训练他们自己的系统，这一过程被称为蒸馏。 虽然提炼是全球人工智能实验室在一定程度上的常见做法，但这些公司表示，他们的模型已经受到查询的轰炸，以收获高级推理。白宫四月份警告说，中国正在以“工业规模”这样做。 北京方面予以反击，否认这些指控毫无根据，并称美国威胁实施制裁和示范禁令是“技术欺凌”，旨在遏制中国的崛起。 华盛顿智库史汀生中心战略远见中心的研究分析师朱莉娅·尼赫（Giulia Neaher）淡化了提炼在基米进步中的作用。 “[其成功]很大程度上归功于为建设这个项目而投入的人才、基础设施和资源......

title.en: Gina Rinehart funded flights and fashion show for Pauline Hanson
title.zh: 吉娜·莱因哈特 (Gina Rinehart) 资助宝琳·汉森 (Pauline Hanson) 的航班和时装秀

summary.en: While Gina Rinehart supported her trip, the One Nation leader said she paid for accommodation, meals and daily expenses.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Mining magnate Gina Rinehart flew One Nation leader Pauline Hanson around Europe and paid for her tickets to a luxury fashion show while she was there.

Hanson's flights from London to Sicily via Rome, and back again, were all funded by Rinehart, the senator's parliamentary register of interests revealed after being updated on Tuesday.

However, Hanson reported paying for accommodation, meals and daily expenses herself during the July 11 to 16 trip, as first reported by Fairfax outlets.

Hanson drew criticism after she and Rinehart were sighted at a luxury Italian resort and attending a Dolce & Gabbana fashion event in Sicily.

Questioned when she returned to Australia, Senator Hanson did not go into detail on how the bill was split, but insisted taxpayers had not paid for the luxury weekend.

"It didn't cost the taxpayer one cent for my trip overseas. Not one cent," she told a Seven West Media event.

Hanson, who was also gifted a private plane by Rinehart in April, defended her billionaire friend, who inherited Hancock Prospecting from her late father, saying she had "done it tough".

"She had to borrow everything and was flat out in the very start to pay the bills. She's built up that company," she said.

On Monday, Hanson lost an appeal over a Federal Court finding she had made a racist remark towards deputy Greens leader Mehreen Faruqi.

In response to a post on social media soon after the death of Queen Elizabeth II in 2022, Hanson told Faruqi to "piss off back to Pakistan".

In his initial decision handed down in 2024, Justice Angus Stewart ruled the post was "seriously offensive" and a "strong form of racism".

Hanson said she was disappointed by Monday's outcome and was considering lodging a final appeal in the High Court.

"Public discussion in Australia has become almost totally silenced by laws and rules which prevent ordinary people expressing their personal views in case some small part of our society takes some sort of offence or feels hurt or 'distressed'," she said in a statement.

title.en: Australia's favourite date to tie the knot — and what fresh marriage data reveals
title.zh: 澳大利亚人最喜欢的结婚日期——以及新的婚姻数据揭示了什么

summary.en: New data indicates a decline in marriage rates across Australia, accompanied by a slight increase in the divorce rate.
summary.zh: 新数据显示，澳大利亚的结婚率有所下降，而离婚率则略有上升。

body.en:
Saturday 25 October was Australia's favourite day to say "I do" in 2025 — but new data suggests fewer couples are saying it.

Fewer Australians tied the knot last year than the year before, according to new figures from the Australian Bureau of Statistics.

At the same time, more marriages are coming to an end, with the divorce rate ticking upward for the first time in several years, though ultimately remaining lower than it was 20 years ago.

The most popular wedding date in 2025 was Saturday 25 October — i.e. the symmetrical 25/10/25 — with 2,035 marriages.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

That's about 500 more than the runner-up, Saturday 22 November (22/11/25) — which had 1,527.

ABS data show there's somewhat of a trend towards more marriages on dates with numerical significance, though for some it could also be coincidence.

The least popular days were Christmas Day, with 51 weddings, Boxing Day with 54, New Year's Day with 57, and Tuesday 29 July with 61.

Spring dominated the wedding calendar, with most of the top ten dates falling in September, October and November. The rest were scattered across autumn.

Saturday remains, unsurprisingly, the nation's preferred wedding day — more than 52,000 marriages took place on a Saturday in 2025, and 45 of the year's most popular dates fell on one.

Friday came in second, with just over 21,000 marriages, led by Friday 10 October (10/10/25).

Zoom out further, and one day still reigns supreme: 10 November 2012 — the sequential 10/11/12.

That remains the most popular wedding date of the past 20 years, with 3,081 marriages recorded on that day — still comfortably ahead of the runner-up, 11 November 2011 (11/11/11), which had 2,614.

Beyond the calendar quirks, the broader numbers tell a clearer story: marriage is becoming less common in Australia.

There were 118,804 marriages registered in 2025 — 2,040 fewer than in 2024, a drop of 1.7 per cent.

That's in line with 2023's total (118,439), but still well above the pandemic-era lows of 2020 and 2021.

Adjusted for population, the marriage rate — the number of marriages per 1,000 people aged 16 and over — fell slightly to 5.3 in 2025, down from 5.5 in both 2023 and 2024.

Zoom out to 2005, where the marriage rate was 6.9, and the decline is even more stark.

The biggest drops came among 25-29 and 30-34 year-olds. No age group recorded an increase.

Despite the falling numbers, the age at which Australians marry has barely moved: 32.7 years for men (down marginally from 32.8 in 2024) and 31.2 years for women, unchanged for the third year running.

summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及真理、分辨与诚实。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Almost one million Origin Energy customers had their details accessed by hackers after a major data breach last week, the company has revealed.

On Tuesday, Origin said it had completed an initial review into the incident and identified that approximately 900,000 current and former customers' data was accessed by the hackers.

"To our customers, I am sorry. We don't take for granted the trust customers place in Origin and our safeguarding of their information," CEO Frank Calabria said in a statement.

Last week, the energy company announced it was the victim of the security incident , saying names, addresses, dates of birth, phone numbers and account information could all have been viewed.

Other potential details include the last four digits of credit cards, or the last three digits of bank accounts.

The company said it would be contacting affected customers first and was opening up a dedicated hotline for those concerned.

Origin said it had been trying to confirm the credibility of the threat since early July.

"We worked to confirm its credibility and potential impact; however, based on the information available, it was not assessed to be credible," Calabria said.

"On 22 July, new information emerged that indicated a potential security incident may have occurred. We acted immediately, providing updates to the market and notifying our customers as a precaution."

Origin, which has 4.8 million customer accounts in Australia and provides electricity, natural gas, LPG and internet services, said last week it did not believe the data obtained included credit card or bank details.

The company has also warned customers to be alert to a greater risk of scams that could arise from the data breach, advising customers to be wary of unexpected calls, emails or texts referring to their account.

Those who get such contact should independently contact Origin through numbers on official channels, it said, and do not provide passwords or personal information to anyone.

"We are acutely aware that others may exploit this incident, including by impersonating Origin or through other scam activity," Calabria said.

"We recommend that all our customers remain vigilant to suspicious activity and a heightened risk of scams.

Griffith University's Graeme Hughes, an expert on business and consumer issues, said the breach was unlikely to cause cases of payment fraud but marked a "social engineering problem".

title.en: ACTU leaders Sally McManus and Michele O'Neil to step aside for 'new generation'
title.zh: ACTU 领导人莎莉·麦克马纳斯 (Sally McManus) 和米歇尔·奥尼尔 (Michele O'Neil) 为“新一代”让位

summary.en: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese thanked the pair for their "tireless advocacy" for workers.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Australia's most powerful union figures have stepped down after almost a decade, saying a new generation of leaders was needed amid ongoing turbulence in the movement.

Sally McManus has been secretary of the Australian Council of Trade Unions (ACTU) since 2017, and Michele O'Neil its president since 2018.

The pair announced on Monday that they would leave their posts, making way for younger leaders to "take (the) movement forward".

''The ACTU's union affiliates will decide on the next leadership team, initially with the ACTU Executive filling the casual vacancies and then through an election at next year's congress, which will coincide with the ACTU's 100th anniversary," the pair said in a statement.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

McManus will finish in the role at the end of August, while O'Neil will depart before the end of the year to ''assist with the leadership transition''.

While the pair have been praised for their work in securing deals for workers, the ACTU has been plagued by difficulties after alleged infiltration of criminals in the Construction, Forestry and Maritime Employees Union (CMFEU).

In 2024, McManus denied she knew of any of the behaviour in the Victorian branch, and also oversaw the ACTU's suspension of CFMEU divisions while it sorted itself out.

It was "essential" the sector emerged from that turbulent period under new leadership, O'Neil told ABC RN on Tuesday.

"Workers who work in the construction industry around this country, by and large, are hardworking, good people who work in tough and dangerous jobs, and they deserve a great union," she said.

"They deserve a union that is completely free of any violence or corruption or organised crime," she said.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese thanked the pair for their "tireless advocacy" for workers, and their support to him personally.

"It is fitting that Sally and Michele announce they're stepping down from their respective positions at a time when there have been significant wage increases in critical and long-undervalued sectors, the gender pay gap is at a record low and union membership is growing for the first time in decades", he said in a statement.

title.en: 'I'm not Jacinta Allan': Caroll pledges 'new direction' and calls a royal commission
title.zh: “我不是杰辛塔·艾伦”：卡罗尔承诺“新方向”并召集皇家委员会

summary.en: The new premier's predecessor had consistently rejected calls for an inquiry into the state's scandal-plagued construction sector.

body.en:
New Victorian Premier Ben Carroll has declared he will lead his government in a "new direction", while distancing himself from his predecessors Jacinta Allan and Daniel Andrews.

In his first comments after being elected state Labor leader, Carroll also announced a royal commission into the construction sector, which has been marred by corruption allegations, and the strengthening of Victoria's anti-corruption watchdog.

"Let me make one thing very clear: I am not Daniel Andrews. I am not Jacinta Allan," he said on Tuesday afternoon, just hours after Allan's resignation.

The former deputy premier said "circumstances changed" in the six weeks since he promised Allan he would not challenge her for the top job. He thanked Allan for her service to the Labor Party and the state.

Carroll was elected to the top job after a chaotic party room meeting triggered by Allan's resignation, following her loss of party support amid dire polling.

Polls showed voters are frustrated with the high cost of living, rising state debt, infrastructure delays and alleged corruption on the state's Big Build projects.

Carroll was expected to secure the leadership unopposed before Victorian Attorney-General Sonya Kilkenny mounted a late challenge.

Under Labor rules, a contested leadership ballot must be put to a vote of the party's rank-and-file members.

The process could take weeks and would plunge the government into political instability just months before the November state election.

But after a lengthy meeting, during which both yelling and cheering could be heard at various stages, Carroll emerged as premier. State Transport Minister Gabrielle Williams was elected his deputy.

Announcing her resignation on Tuesday morning, Allan said it had been an honour to serve as leader.

"Thank you to the Victorian people. It has been the honour of my life to serve you as your premier. I stepped down after 1,036 days in this role. Not one of them wasted, not one of them easy."

Allan said she believed she would have won a rank-and-file membership vote, but said the process would have been damaging in the lead-up to the November election.

"More importantly, it puts the state in a position of uncertainty. That hurts the Victorian people, and I just won't do that. At the end of the day, I am, and always have been, a team player."

Allan reflected on her nearly three years as premier, saying her biggest priority had been tackling the cost of living.
